reason: The cited evidence supports that laser-clad HEAs can achieve metallurgical bonding, high hardness, and good wear resistance, but neither passage addresses hot-cracking mitigation, HAZ reduction, or comparative cracking resistance versus fusion welding, leaving the core premises about cracking unsupported.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a metallurgically bonded HEA overlay with low dilution and fast solidification
HEA coatings (e.g., FeCoCrNiAl-based) can provide high hardness and elevated-temperature wear resistance
Laser cladding with controlled heat input and rapid solidification minimizes the HAZ and avoids brittle interdendritic phases
The deposited HEA overlay will exhibit fewer hot-cracking defects than traditional fusion-welding repairs
